items.name: Theorem 1.0.1 (the unbounded denominators conjecture)
items.statement: Let N ≥ 1 and let f(τ) ∈ ℤ[[q^{1/N}]], q = exp(πiτ), be holomorphic on the upper half plane ℍ. Suppose there are k ∈ ℤ and a finite-index subgroup Γ ⊂ SL₂(ℤ) with f((aτ+b)/(cτ+d)) = (cτ+d)^k f(τ) for all (a b; c d) ∈ Γ, and that f is meromorphic at the cusps (it extends meromorphically near every cusp of the compactification of ℍ/Γ). Then f is a modular form for a congruence subgroup of SL₂(ℤ). Contrapositive: a modular form in ℚ[[q^{1/N}]] that is not modular for any congruence subgroup has unbounded denominators.
items.locator: Theorem 1.0.1, p.627; proof assembled in §6.3, pp.685–686 (JAMS 38 (2025))
items.note: The main theorem. §6.3: Theorem 5.1.4 gives hypothesis (1) of Proposition 3.0.1 with A = ζ(3)/2, Theorem 6.0.1 with p(x) = x^N and r = 1 − BN⁻³ gives hypothesis (2); Proposition 3.0.1 then gives [R_{2N} : ℚ(λ)] ≤ CN³ log N and Proposition 4.3.5 gives R_{2N} = M_{2N} for all N. The reduction to weight 0 multiplies by (λ/16η(τ/2)²)^k (p.628). Equivalent reading (p.628): the Belyĭ covers of ℙ¹∖{0,1,∞} with a Puiseux branch in ℤ[[λ(τ/m)/16]] ⊗ ℂ are exactly the congruence covers ℍ/Γ → ℍ/Γ(2). No library or atlas layer states it. Routed to the new Part II NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Remarks 6.3.1–6.3.2 (algebraic-integer Fourier coefficients)
items.statement: If f(τ) is a modular form of integral weight for a finite-index subgroup of SL₂(ℤ), meromorphic at all cusps, whose Fourier expansion at one cusp lies in ℤ̄[[q^{1/N}]] (algebraic-integer coefficients), then f is a modular form for a congruence subgroup. Proof 1 (Remark 6.3.1): run §§3–6 over a number field K with f ∈ O_K[[q^{1/N}]], using V(U, x(t), O_K) = V(U, x(t), ℤ) ⊗_ℚ K. Proof 2 (Remark 6.3.2, Voight): for a ℤ-basis α₁,…,α_d of O_K apply Theorem 1.0.1 to f_i := Tr_{K/ℚ}(α_i f) ∈ ℤ[[q^{1/N}]] and intersect the congruence subgroups.
items.locator: Remarks 6.3.1 and 6.3.2, pp.685–686; sentence after Theorem 1.0.1, p.627 (JAMS 38 (2025))
items.note: Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Shimura's theorem: congruence modular forms with rational coefficients have bounded denominators
items.statement: If f is a holomorphic modular form of weight k for Γ(M) whose Fourier expansion at i∞ has coefficients in ℚ, then there is D ≥ 1 with D·f ∈ ℤ[[q^{1/M}]] ([Shi71, Theorem 3.52]). Consequently (proof of Lemma 4.2.2) every holomorphic modular function on Y(2N) with rational coefficients at i∞ has bounded denominators: fΔ^m is a holomorphic form with rational coefficients for m ≫ 0 and Δ⁻¹ ∈ q⁻²ℤ[[q]].
items.locator: p.628 (the converse direction, citing [Shi59], [Shi71, Theorem 3.52], [Kat73, §1.2]); proof of Lemma 4.2.2, p.655 (JAMS 38 (2025))
items.note: Not planned: the integrated decomposition of AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights imports Shimura Thm 3.52 without planning it (node R15.6/residual-modularity…, hypothesis 4), and records the finite freeness of the Deligne–Serre module as a gap. R15.2 plans the integral q-expansion principle over ℤ[1/n] and finite generation, which gives bounded denominators away from the level; the statement here also bounds denominators at primes dividing the level. Routed as a source of AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights R15.2.

items.name: Modular forms and modular functions for finite-index subgroups, meromorphic at the cusps
items.statement: For a finite-index Γ ⊂ SL₂(ℤ) and k ∈ ℤ: a holomorphic f : ℍ → ℂ with f|_kγ = f for γ ∈ Γ that is meromorphic at every cusp (its expansion in the local parameter at each cusp has finitely many negative terms). A holomorphic modular function is the case k = 0 (poles allowed only at cusps); f is a holomorphic modular form when it is holomorphic at the cusps. The paper uses both q = e^{πiτ} (default) and q = e^{2πiτ}.
items.locator: Theorem 1.0.1, p.627; Definition 4.2.1, p.655; Definition 7.4.3, p.692 (JAMS 38 (2025))
items.note: Near miss: Mathlib's `ModularForm Γ k` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Basic.lean:74) is holomorphic and bounded at every cusp of a subgroup Γ of GL(2,ℝ); forms meromorphic at the cusps (weakly holomorphic) and modular functions with poles at cusps are absent. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Congruence subgroups Γ(N), Γ₀(p), Γ₁(p)
items.statement: Γ(N) = ker(SL₂(ℤ) → SL₂(ℤ/N)), Γ₀(p) (lower-left entry ≡ 0 mod p), Γ₁(p) (≡ (1 * ; 0 1) mod p); a subgroup of SL₂(ℤ) is congruence if it contains some Γ(N); E = {±I} and ⟨E, Γ(N)⟩ its product with Γ(N).
items.note: Read at 082e2d3: Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/CongruenceSubgroups.lean:41, 79, 131, 163 (`IsCongruenceSubgroup Γ := ∃ N ≠ 0, Gamma N ≤ Γ`).

items.name: q-expansions at i∞ in fractional powers of q
items.statement: For f invariant under τ ↦ τ + h, its expansion in the local parameter exp(2πiτ/h) at i∞; in the paper f ∈ ℤ[[q^{1/N}]] or ℚ((q^{1/N})) with q = e^{πiτ}.
items.note: Read at 082e2d3: Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/QExpansion.lean:162 (`qExpansion h f`, the power series whose m-th coefficient is the Taylor coefficient of the cusp function at q = 0, q = exp(2πiτ/h)). Laurent expansions with negative powers are not covered (see modular-forms-finite-index).

items.name: Dedekind η, the discriminant Δ and E₂
items.statement: η(τ) = q^{1/24}∏(1 − qⁿ) with q = e^{2πiτ}; Δ = η²⁴ = q∏(1 − qⁿ)²⁴; E₂ the weight-2 Eisenstein series, with θΔ = E₂Δ for θ = q d/dq.
items.note: Read at 082e2d3: DedekindEta.lean:60 (η), Discriminant.lean:52 (Δ = η²⁴), EisensteinSeries/E2/Defs.lean:60 (E₂), DedekindEta.lean:169 (logDeriv η = (πi/12)E₂, which gives θΔ = E₂Δ).

items.name: Jacobi theta functions ϑ₂, ϑ₃, ϑ₄ and their eta-quotient forms
items.statement: With q = e^{πiτ}: ϑ₂ = Σ q^{(n+1/2)²} = 2η²(2τ)/η(τ), ϑ₃ = Σ q^{n²} = η⁵(τ)/(η²(τ/2)η²(2τ)), ϑ₄ = Σ(−1)ⁿq^{n²} = η²(τ/2)/η(τ) (Jacobi's triple product); they are weight-1/2 forms without zeros on ℍ, and even-degree Laurent monomials ϑ₂^aϑ₃^bϑ₄^c lie in the quasi-modular ring for Γ(12).
items.note: QM.1 constructs theta and eta functions with their multiplier systems; QM.0 the product identities. Mathlib has ϑ₃ as `jacobiTheta τ = Σ exp(πi n² τ)` (JacobiTheta/OneVariable.lean:29) and η; Jacobi's triple product is not in Mathlib.

items.name: The modular λ-function (Legendre's parameter)
items.statement: λ(τ)/16 = (η(τ/2)η(2τ)²/η(τ)³)⁸ = q∏_{n≥1}((1 + q^{2n})/(1 + q^{2n−1}))⁸ = q − 8q² + 44q³ − ⋯ with q = e^{πiτ}; equivalently λ = (ϑ₂/ϑ₃)⁴. λ is a Hauptmodul for Γ(2), and weight-0 holomorphic modular forms on Y(2) are ℚ[λ, 1/λ, 1/(1−λ)].
items.note: Not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti. ConformalMapping's document assigns the λ-covering ℍ/Γ(2) ≅ ℂ∖{0,1} to ModularForms, and BelyiMaps records it as modular-forms material, but no ModularForms layer plans it. Identities checked here by exact q-series arithmetic to q²⁹. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: λ : ℍ → ℂ∖{0,1} is the universal covering, with deck group Γ(2)/{±1}
items.statement: λ induces ℍ/Γ(2) ≅ ℂ∖{0,1} = Y(2) and is a holomorphic covering map; for every finite-index Γ ⊂ Γ(2), ℍ/Γ → Y(2) is a finite étale cover (a Belyĭ map after compactification), so every modular function for Γ is an algebraic function of λ branched only over λ = 0, 1, ∞, and every holomorphic disc in Y(2) lifts to ℍ/Γ.
items.note: Tau Ceti has the topological universal cover (AlgebraicTopology/UniversalCover/Basic.lean:66), the Riemann mapping theorem, Schwarz reflection and the monodromy theorem (ConformalMapping L3–L4 done); the λ-covering itself is unplanned (see lambda-function). Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: ℤ[[q]] = ℤ[[λ/16]] and the Kummer integrality of (λ/16)^{1/N}
items.statement: With x := λ(τ)/16 ∈ q + q²ℤ[[q]] (q = e^{πiτ}) the formal inverse is q = x + 8x² + 84x³ + 992x⁴ + ⋯ ∈ x + x²ℤ[[x]], so ℤ[[q]] = ℤ[[x]]; for N ≥ 1 and t = q^{1/N}, x_N := (λ(τ)/16)^{1/N} ∈ t + t²ℤ[1/N][[t]] while x_N^N = λ/16 ∈ ℤ[[t^N]] (3.0.2).
items.note: Coefficients 1, 8, 84, 992, 12514, … checked here by series reversion. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Lemma 1.1.2 (an integral power series convergent beyond the unit disc is a polynomial)
items.statement: If f(x) = Σ aₙxⁿ ∈ ℤ[[x]] defines a holomorphic function on D(0, R) for some R > 1, then f is a polynomial (Liouville lower bound |aₙ| ≥ 1 for aₙ ≠ 0 against the Cauchy bound |aₙ| = o(ηⁿ), 1 > η > 1/R).
items.note: The model of the Liouville/Cauchy tension. Routed to ArithmeticAlgebraizationAndHolonomyBounds.

items.name: André's algebraicity criterion (the case used here)
items.statement: [And04, Théorème 5.4.3], special case: if f ∈ ℤ[[x]] and there is a holomorphic φ : (D(0,1), 0) → (ℂ, 0) with |φ′(0)| > 1 such that f(φ(z)) converges on D(0,1) (a simultaneous analytic uniformization of x and f), then f is algebraic over ℚ(x).
items.note: Recovered by Theorem 2.0.1 applied to the powers of f; example f = (1 − m²x)^{1/m}, φ(z) = (1 − e^{Mz})/m² (p.630); the 1/16 theorem of Carathéodory follows (p.631). Routed to ArithmeticAlgebraizationAndHolonomyBounds.

items.name: Jacobi's formula ₂F₁(½,½;1;λ) = ϑ₃² (the transcendental boundary case)
items.statement: F(x) := ₂F₁(½, ½; 1; 16x) = Σ_{n≥0} C(2n,n)² xⁿ ∈ ℤ[[x]], and with x = λ(τ)/16, F = (Σ_{n∈ℤ} q^{n²})², a weight-one modular form for Γ(2); F is holonomic on ℂ∖{0, 1/16} with infinite local monodromy at x = 0 (continuation around x = 1/16 produces a log x term), so it is transcendental.
items.note: Mathlib has ₂F₁ (SpecialFunctions/OrdinaryHypergeometric.lean:81) and ϑ₃; the identity is absent. Checked here to q¹³. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Example (1.0.3): j^{1/3} is a congruence Hauptmodul
items.statement: With q = e^{2πiτ}: j^{1/3} = q^{−1/3}(1 + 240Σσ₃(n)qⁿ)/∏(1 − qⁿ)⁸ = q^{−1/3}(1 + 248q + 4124q² + 34752q³ + ⋯) has integer coefficients and is a Hauptmodul for the level-3 subgroup equal to the kernel of PSL₂(ℤ) → PSL₂(𝔽₃) ≅ A₄ → ℤ/3 (apply Theorem 1.0.1 to j^{1/3}Δ); its coefficients are graded dimensions of the level-one E₈⁽¹⁾ module.
items.note: An acceptance example. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Example (1.0.4): the roots h^{1/n} of h = λ(1−λ)/16
items.statement: h := λ(1−λ)/16 = (η(τ/2)η(2τ)/η(τ)²)²⁴ = q∏((1+q^{2n})/(1+qⁿ))²⁴ is a modular function for Γ₀(2) ⊃ Γ(2); h^{1/n} has bounded denominators iff it is congruence iff n | 24, because Γ₀(2) (in PSL₂(ℤ)) has abelianization ℤ ⊕ ℤ/2 while its congruence completion has abelianization ℤ/24 ⊕ ℤ/2; the other ℤ/2 gives √(1 − 64h) = 1 − 2λ.
items.note: The product formula was checked here to q²⁹. An acceptance example. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Klein's theorem via integrality: noncongruence Fermat curves
items.statement: (λ/16)^{1/8} = q^{1/8}∏(1+q^{2n})(1+q^{2n−1})⁻¹ ∈ ℤ[[q^{1/8}]] and x⁸ + y⁸ = 1 is congruence, whereas for n ∉ {1, 2, 4, 8} the affine Fermat curve xⁿ + yⁿ = 1 has noncongruence Fuchsian group, detected by (1 − x)^{1/n} ∉ ℤ[[x/16]] ⊗ ℂ ([KF17, p.534]).
items.note: An acceptance example. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Theorem 2.0.1 (arithmetic holonomicity bound)
items.statement: Data: (i) p(x) ∈ ℚ(x)∖ℚ with no pole at 0; (ii) x(t) ∈ t + t²ℚ[[t]] with x*p := p(x(t)) ∈ ℤ[[t]]; (iii) φ holomorphic on a neighbourhood of the closed disc D̄(0,1), φ(0) = 0, |φ′(0)| > 1, with φ*p ∈ O(D̄(0,1)). If f₁,…,f_m ∈ ℚ[[x]] are ℚ(p(x))-linearly independent with x*f_i ∈ ℤ[[t]] and φ*f_i ∈ O(D̄(0,1)), then m ≤ e·∫_𝕋 log⁺|p∘φ| dμ_Haar / log|φ′(0)|, e = 2.718….
items.note: The integrated (mean) growth term in the numerator, rather than a supremum, is the novelty. Bost–Charles [BC22, Cor. 8.3.5] later improved e to 2 (Remark 2.5.29). Routed to ArithmeticAlgebraizationAndHolonomyBounds.

items.name: Theorem 2.0.1, algebraicity clause
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 2.0.1 each f_i is algebraic: f_i ∈ ℚ̄(x) ∩ ℚ[[x]] (apply the bound to the powers f_i^N, which keep x*f_i^N ∈ ℤ[[t]] and φ*f_i^N ∈ O(D̄(0,1))).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticAlgebraizationAndHolonomyBounds.

items.name: Definition 2.0.4: the ring H(U, x(t), R) and the space V(U, x(t), R)
items.statement: For U ⊂ ℂ open, R ⊂ ℂ a subring with fraction field F and x(t) ∈ tℚ[[t]]: H(U, x(t), R) is the ring of f(x) ∈ F[[x]] with f(x(t)) ∈ R[[t]] such that some nonzero linear differential operator L over ℚ̄(x) has L(f) = 0 and trivial local monodromy at every singular point of L in U; V(U, x(t), R) is the F(x)-span of H(U, x(t), R); H(U, R) := H(U, t, R), V(U, R) := V(U, t, R).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticAlgebraizationAndHolonomyBounds.

items.name: Trivial local monodromy of a linear differential operator at a point
items.statement: A linear operator L of order n has trivial local monodromy at α if there are a neighbourhood U_α ∋ α and meromorphic g₁,…,g_n on U_α forming a ℂ-basis of the solutions of L(f) = 0 on U_α∖{α}; this holds at nonsingular points; example L = x d/dx − n (n ∈ ℤ∖{0}) at 0, with solutions ℂ·xⁿ.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticAlgebraizationAndHolonomyBounds.

items.name: Corollary 2.0.5 (finite-dimensionality of V(U, ℤ))
items.statement: Let 0 ∈ U ⊂ ℂ be open. If the uniformization radius of the pointed Riemann surface (U, 0) is strictly greater than 1, then V(U, ℤ) is finite-dimensional over ℚ(x).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticAlgebraizationAndHolonomyBounds.

items.name: Corollary 2.0.5 (the holonomy rank bound (2.0.7))
items.statement: Let p(x) ∈ ℚ(x)∖ℚ have no poles in U, φ : D̄(0,1) → U holomorphic with φ(0) = 0 and |φ′(0)| > 1, and x(t) ∈ t + t²ℚ[[t]] with p(x(t)) ∈ ℤ[[t]]. Then dim_{ℚ(p(x))} V(U, x(t), ℤ) ≤ e·∫_𝕋 log⁺|p∘φ| dμ_Haar / log|φ′(0)|.
items.note: Proof: Cauchy's theorem on linear ODEs gives g ∈ ℚ̄[p(x)]∖{0} with φ*(gf) ∈ O(D̄(0,1)); then Theorem 2.0.1. Routed to ArithmeticAlgebraizationAndHolonomyBounds.

items.name: Cauchy's theorem for linear ODEs with analytic coefficients, and removing singularities with trivial local monodromy
items.statement: Solutions of a linear ODE with coefficients holomorphic on a domain continue analytically along every path in it, and on a simply connected domain without singular points form an n-dimensional space of holomorphic functions; at a singular point α (algebraic, for coefficients in ℚ̄(x)) with trivial local monodromy there is g ∈ ℚ̄[p(x)]∖{0} with g·h holomorphic at α for every local solution h.
items.note: Tau Ceti has analytic continuation along paths (Analysis/Complex/Conformal/Continuation/Basic.lean:190) and the monodromy theorem, Mathlib has Picard–Lindelöf for real ODEs; the complex linear ODE existence and continuation theorem is absent. Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution, which also needs it for Lemma 5.1.8.

items.name: Lemma 2.0.8 (the bound with a holomorphic multiplier)
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 2.0.1, for every h holomorphic on a neighbourhood of D̄(0,1) with h(0) = 1: m ≤ e·max{sup_𝕋 log|h|, sup_𝕋 log|h·φ*p|} / log|φ′(0)|, and f₁,…,f_m ∈ ℚ̄(x) ∩ ℚ[[x]]. By Remark 2.3.3 the infimum of this bound over h is the bound (2.0.3).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticAlgebraizationAndHolonomyBounds.

items.name: Lemma 2.1.2 (the auxiliary construction in d variables)
items.statement: Let d, α ∈ ℕ_{>0}, κ ∈ (0,1). As α → ∞ with d, κ fixed there is F(x) = Σ_{i∈{1..m}^d, k∈{0..D−1}^d} a_{i,k} p(x)^k ∏_s f_{i_s}(x_s) ∈ ℚ[[x]]∖{0} (x = (x₁,…,x_d), p(x)^k = ∏ p(x_j)^{k_j}) vanishing to order ≥ α at 0, with (1) D ≤ (d!)^{−1/d}(1/m)(1 + 1/κ)^{1/d} α + o(α), and (2) a_{i,k} ∈ ℤ with |a_{i,k}| ≤ exp(κCα + o(α)), C depending only on the radius ρ of (2.1.1) and on the degree and height of p.
items.note: Uses Siegel's lemma and the denominator lemma; nonvanishing uses the ℚ(p(x))-independence of the products ∏ f_{i_s}(x_s) by induction on d. Routed to ArithmeticAlgebraizationAndHolonomyBounds.

items.name: Denominators of the inverse series (proof of Lemma 2.1.2)
items.statement: If p ∈ ℚ(x)∖ℚ has no pole at 0 and x(t) ∈ t + t²ℚ[[t]] with p(x(t)) ∈ ℤ[[t]], then x(t) ∈ t + (t²/M)ℤ[[t/M]] for some M ∈ ℕ_{>0} bounded in terms of the degree and height of p (explicitly M = c²N⁴M₁², from Eisenstein's theorem and (1 + u)^{1/N} ∈ ℤ[[u/N²]]); then t(x) ∈ x + (x²/M)ℤ[[x/M]] and each f_i ∈ ℤ[[x/M]].
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticAlgebraizationAndHolonomyBounds.

items.name: Eisenstein's theorem on algebraic power series
items.statement: A Puiseux branch y ∈ ℚ̄[[x^{1/N}]] algebraic over ℚ(x) has y ∈ ℤ̄[[x^{1/N}/M₁]] for some M₁ ∈ ℕ_{>0} ([BG06, §11.4]).
items.note: Not in Mathlib. Routed to ArithmeticAlgebraizationAndHolonomyBounds.

items.name: Siegel's lemma
items.statement: A system A·t = 0 of m homogeneous linear equations in n > m unknowns with integer coefficients has a nonzero integer solution with ‖t‖ ≤ (n·max(1, ‖A‖))^{m/(n−m)} ([BG06, Lemma 2.9.1]).
items.note: Read at 082e2d3: Mathlib/NumberTheory/SiegelsLemma.lean:155, for card α < card β, ∃ t ≠ 0, A *ᵥ t = 0 ∧ ‖t‖ ≤ (n·max 1 ‖A‖)^{m/(n−m)}.

items.name: Stirling's formula (d/(d!)^{1/d} → e)
items.statement: d/(d!)^{1/d} → e as d → ∞, which turns the constant (d/(d!)^{1/d})(1 + 1/κ)^{1/d} of §2.2 into e.
items.note: Read at 082e2d3: Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Stirling.lean:238.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.1 (Nevanlinna's quotient representation)
items.statement: For ε > 0 and g holomorphic on a neighbourhood of D̄(0,1), there is h holomorphic on a neighbourhood of D̄(0,1) with h(0) = 1 and max{sup_𝕋 log|h|, sup_𝕋 log|hg|} ≤ ∫_𝕋 log⁺|g| dμ_Haar + ε. Conversely (Remark 2.3.3) every h with h(0) = 1 has max{sup_𝕋 log|h|, sup_𝕋 log|hg|} ≥ ∫_𝕋 log⁺|g| dμ_Haar.
items.note: Proof: divide by the Blaschke product of the zeros, write log|G| by the Poisson kernel on |z| ≤ r, let r → 1, then rescale to a slightly larger disc. Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Blaschke products
items.statement: For zeros a₁,…,a_k in D̄(0,1) with multiplicities n_i, B(z) = ∏((z − a_i)/(1 − ā_i z))^{n_i} is a holomorphic self-map of D(0,1) preserving 𝕋, and g/B is holomorphic and zero-free on D(0,1).
items.note: Not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (Tau Ceti has disc automorphisms). Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Herglotz representation of log g for a zero-free g ((2.3.2), (6.1.9)–(6.1.11))
items.statement: If g is holomorphic and zero-free on a neighbourhood of D̄(0,R) with g(0) = 1, then for |z| < R: log g(z) = ∫_{|w|=R} log|g(w)|·(w+z)/(w−z) dμ_Haar(w) and g′(z)/g(z) = ∫_{|w|=R} (2w/(w−z)²) log|g(w)| dμ_Haar(w).
items.note: Near miss: Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Poisson.lean:253 gives f(w) = circleAverage((Re H)·f) for f holomorphic (H the Herglotz–Riesz kernel) and :302 differentiates the Herglotz integral; the representation of a holomorphic function by the Herglotz integral of its real part is not stated. Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Lemma 2.4.2 (the lexicographically lowest coefficient)
items.statement: If G ∈ ℂ[[z₁,…,z_d]]∖{0} is holomorphic on a neighbourhood of the closed unit polydisc and c zⁿ is its lexicographically minimal monomial, then log|c| ≤ ∫_{𝕋^d} log|G| dμ_Haar.
items.note: d = 1 is Jensen's formula; the induction integrates over the remaining variables (plurisubharmonicity). Routed to ArithmeticAlgebraizationAndHolonomyBounds.

items.name: Jensen's formula on a closed disc
items.statement: For f meromorphic on D̄(c, R): the circle average of log|f| over |z − c| = R equals Σ_u div_f(u) log(R/|c − u|) + div_f(c) log R + log|trailing coefficient of f at c|; for analytic f with f(c) ≠ 0, ∫ log|f| = Σ log(R/|c−u|) + log|f(c)| over the zeros u. Used for d = 1 in Lemma 2.4.2 and as the Poisson–Jensen formula behind (6.1.4).
items.locator: proof of Lemma 2.4.2, p.642; proof of Lemma 6.1.2, p.680 (JAMS 38 (2025))
items.note: Read at 082e2d3: Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/JensenFormula.lean:308 and :376 (hypothesis MeromorphicOn f (closedBall c |R|)).

items.name: Lemma 2.5.3 (Fekete)
items.statement: sup_{z∈𝕋^d} |V(z)| = sup ∏_{i<j}|z_i − z_j| = d^{d/2}, with equality exactly when z₁,…,z_d are the vertices of a regular d-gon (V the Vandermonde determinant (2.5.2); proof by Hadamard's inequality).
items.note: Mathlib has the Vandermonde determinant (LinearAlgebra/Vandermonde.lean:219) but not Hadamard's inequality. Routed to ArithmeticAlgebraizationAndHolonomyBounds.

items.name: Definition 2.5.4 (box discrepancy on the circle)
items.statement: D(z₁,…,z_d) := sup over circular arcs I ⊂ 𝕋 of |μ_Haar(I) − #{i : z_i ∈ I}/d| ∈ (0,1].
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticAlgebraizationAndHolonomyBounds.

items.name: Definition 2.5.5 (total variation on the circle)
items.statement: V(g) := sup over 0 ≤ θ₁ < ⋯ < θ_n < 1 of Σ_{j=1}^{n−1} |g(e^{2πiθ_{j+1}}) − g(e^{2πiθ_j})| for g : 𝕋 → ℝ.
items.note: Read at 082e2d3: Mathlib/Topology/EMetricSpace/BoundedVariation.lean:61; V(g) is eVariationOn (θ ↦ g(e^{2πiθ})) on [0,1). The formula V(g) = ∫_𝕋|g′| for g ∈ C¹(𝕋) is stated with Koksma's inequality (item koksma).

items.name: Koksma's inequality (2.5.7) and the C¹ variation formula (2.5.6)
items.statement: For g : 𝕋 → ℝ of bounded variation and z₁,…,z_d ∈ 𝕋: |(1/d)Σ g(z_j) − ∫_𝕋 g dμ_Haar| ≤ V(g)·D(z₁,…,z_d) ([DT97, Thm 1.14]); for g ∈ C¹(𝕋), V(g) = ∫_𝕋 |g′| dμ_Haar, and V(log⁺|h|) < ∞ for h ∈ C¹(𝕋).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticAlgebraizationAndHolonomyBounds.

items.name: The Erdős–Turán inequality (2.5.8)
items.note: Used only for the heuristic remark that poorly distributed tuples are rare; not used in the estimates. Routed to ArithmeticAlgebraizationAndHolonomyBounds.

items.name: Lemma 2.5.9 (poorly distributed tuples have tiny Vandermonde)
items.statement: There are c(ε) > 0 and d₀(ε) such that for ε ∈ (0,1], d ≥ d₀(ε) and z ∈ 𝕋^d with D(z) ≥ ε: |V(z)| = ∏_{i<j}|z_i − z_j| < e^{−c(ε)d²}.
items.note: Bilu's equidistribution theorem in disguise; the proof is by compactness of probability measures on 𝕋 and positivity of logarithmic energy. Routed to ArithmeticAlgebraizationAndHolonomyBounds.

items.name: Haar measure is the equilibrium measure of the circle
items.statement: For every probability measure ν on 𝕋, I(ν) = ∫∫ log(1/|z − w|) dν(z) dν(w) ≥ 0 = I(μ_Haar), with equality only for ν = μ_Haar.
items.note: The paper cites the general existence and uniqueness of equilibrium measures; for 𝕋 it follows from I(ν) = Σ_{n≠0} |ν̂(n)|²/(2|n|). Routed to ArithmeticAlgebraizationAndHolonomyBounds.

items.name: Sequential weak-* compactness of probability measures on 𝕋
items.statement: Every sequence of probability measures on 𝕋 has a subsequence converging weak-* to a probability measure (Banach–Alaoglu on C(𝕋)*, separability of C(𝕋), Riesz–Markov–Kakutani).
items.note: Read at 082e2d3: Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Module/WeakDual.lean:369 (sequential Banach–Alaoglu for separable spaces) and MeasureTheory/Integral/RieszMarkovKakutani/Real.lean:345.

items.name: §2.5.27 (potential-theoretic form of the holonomy bound)
items.statement: For compact K ⊂ D̄(0,1) with transfinite diameter d(K) and equilibrium measure μ_K, if log|φ′(0)| + log d(K) > 0 then, under the hypotheses of Corollary 2.0.5, dim_{ℚ(p(x))} V(U, x(t), ℤ) ≤ e·∫_K log⁺|p∘φ| dμ_K / (log|φ′(0)| + log d(K)); K = D̄(0,1) or 𝕋 recovers (2.0.7).
items.note: Stated without detailed proof in the source. Routed to ArithmeticAlgebraizationAndHolonomyBounds, which imports capacity and equilibrium measures of general compact sets rather than defining them.

items.name: Proposition 3.0.1 (the dimension bound for R_{2N})
items.statement: Let F_N : D(0,1) → ℂ∖μ_N be an analytic universal covering with F_N(0) = 0. Suppose (1) |F_N′(0)| ≥ 16^{1/N}(1 + A/N³) asymptotically for some A > 0, and (2) for fixed B > 0, ∫_{|z|=1−BN⁻³} log⁺|F_N| dμ_Haar ≪_B (log N)/N. Then the ℚ(λ)-vector space R_{2N} has dimension at most C N³ log N over ℚ(λ), for an absolute constant C.
items.note: Proof: Corollary 2.0.5 with U = ℂ∖16^{−1/N}μ_N, p(x) = x^N, x(t) = (λ/16)^{1/N}, φ(z) = 16^{−1/N}F_N(rz), r = 1 − AN⁻³/2. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: R_{2N} ⊂ V(ℂ∖16^{−1/N}μ_N, (λ/16)^{1/N}, ℤ)
items.statement: With t = q^{1/N}, U = ℂ∖16^{−1/N}μ_N and x(t) = (λ(q)/16)^{1/N}, every modular function with expansion at i∞ in ℤ[[q^{1/N}]] ⊗ ℚ and cusp widths dividing 2N lies in H(U, x(t), ℤ) ⊗ ℚ: a minimal-order L over ℚ̄(λ) with L(f) = 0 has trivial local monodromy at λ ≠ 0, 1, ∞ (discs lift through the finite étale cover Y → Y(2)), and, since the widths divide 2N, also at x = 0 after pulling back to U.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 3.0.1, p.650; Remark 3.0.6, p.651 (JAMS 38 (2025))
items.note: Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Cusps and cusp widths of a finite-index subgroup of SL₂(ℤ)
items.statement: For G ⊂ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index every ζ ∈ ℙ¹(ℚ) is a cusp; for ζ = M∞ (M ∈ SL₂(ℤ)) the width of ζ is the least m > 0 with ±MU^mM⁻¹ ∈ G, U = (1 1; 0 1). It depends only on the G-orbit of ζ; the stabilizer is E × ℤ or ℤ; and the widths are the ramification indices of X(G) → X(SL₂(ℤ)) over j = ∞.
items.note: FuchsianOrbifolds Layer 3 constructs cusp data with width, and Layer 4 proves e_cusp = w_{Γ′}/w_Γ for finite-index inclusions (here Γ = SL₂(ℤ), all of whose cusps have width 1). Mathlib has the width at ∞ (NumberTheory/ModularForms/Cusps.lean:332) and Tau Ceti the integer width at ∞ (ModularForms/Cusps/Basic.lean:143).

items.name: Definition 4.1.2 (Wohlfahrt level)
items.statement: The level L(G) of a finite-index subgroup G ⊂ SL₂(ℤ) is the least common multiple of its cusp widths ([Woh64]).
items.note: Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Lemma 4.1.3 (level of an intersection)
items.statement: If G, H ⊂ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index, contain E = {±I}, and L(G), L(H) divide N, then every cusp of G ∩ H has width dividing N.
items.note: Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Lemma 4.1.4 (level of the normal core)
items.statement: If G ⊂ SL₂(ℤ) has finite index, contains E and has Wohlfahrt level N, then its normal core N(G) (the largest normal subgroup of SL₂(ℤ) in G) has finite index and L(N(G)) = N.
items.note: Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Lemma 4.1.7 (level under conjugation by A = diag(p, 1))
items.statement: If H ⊂ SL₂(ℤ) has finite index, contains E and L(H) = N, then L(A⁻¹HA ∩ SL₂(ℤ)) divides Np.
items.note: See sourceIssues E4 for a slip in case (2) of the proof. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Wohlfahrt's theorem
items.statement: A congruence subgroup of SL₂(ℤ) of Wohlfahrt level N contains Γ(N); hence the smallest congruence subgroup of level N containing E is ⟨E, Γ(N)⟩ ([Woh64, Theorem 2]).
items.locator: proof of Lemma 4.4.1, p.659; used in the proof of Lemma 4.4.4 (JAMS 38 (2025))
items.note: FuchsianOrbifolds leaves congruence-subgroup arithmetic to the modular-forms roadmap, which does not state it. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Definition 4.2.1(1): the space M_{2N}
items.statement: M_{2N} is the ℚ(λ)-span, inside ℚ((q^{1/N})) with q = e^{πiτ}, of the holomorphic modular functions on Y(2N) = ℍ/⟨E, Γ(2N)⟩ with rational Fourier coefficients at ζ = i∞; M₂ = ℚ(λ).
items.note: Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Definition 4.2.1(2): the space R_{2N}
items.statement: R_{2N} is the ℚ(λ)-span of the holomorphic modular functions (for finite-index subgroups of SL₂(ℤ)) with rational Fourier coefficients, bounded denominators at ζ = i∞ (coefficients in (1/D)ℤ for some D), and cusp widths dividing 2N at every cusp.
items.note: Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Lemma 4.2.2(a): M_{2N} ⊂ R_{2N}
items.statement: Every generator of M_{2N} has bounded denominators and cusp widths dividing 2N, so M_{2N} ⊂ R_{2N}.
items.note: Uses Shimura's bounded-denominators theorem. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Lemma 4.2.2(b): M_{2N} and R_{2N} are finite-dimensional over ℚ(λ)
items.statement: [R_{2N} : ℚ(λ)] < ∞, by Corollary 2.0.5, because the uniformization radius of ℂ∖16^{−1/N}μ_N exceeds 1: the map (λ(z^N)/16)^{1/N} : D(0,1) → ℂ∖16^{−1/N}μ_N is holomorphic with derivative 1 at 0 and is not a covering, so by the Schwarz lemma the universal covering has |derivative| > 1.
items.note: Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Lemma 4.2.3(a): M_{2N}, R_{2N} are fields, with M₂ ⊂ M_{2N} ⊂ R_{2N}
items.statement: M_{2N} and R_{2N} are subrings of the domain ℚ((q^{1/N})) of finite dimension over ℚ(λ), hence fields; R_{2N} is closed under products because G ∩ H has widths dividing 2N (Lemma 4.1.3); the inclusions M₂ → M_{2N} → R_{2N} are injective algebra maps.
items.note: Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Lemma 4.2.3(b): M_{2N} is the function field of Y(2N)/ℚ
items.statement: Y(2N) has a standard model over ℚ (the moduli of elliptic curves C with a symplectic isomorphism C[2N] ≅ ℤ/2N ⊕ μ_{2N}) in which the cusp i∞ is rational and Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) acts on global sections compatibly with q-expansions; M_{2N} is its function field.
items.note: R12.4 identifies the fixed-pairing twisted curve with its analytic quotient; R15.1 plans the coefficient-field and q-expansion comparisons between algebraic and analytic forms.

items.name: Lemma 4.2.3(c): the group G_{2N} fixing R_{2N}
items.statement: R_{2N} is invariant under a normal finite-index subgroup G_{2N} ⊂ ⟨E, Γ(2N)⟩ of SL₂(ℤ) containing E with L(G_{2N}) = 2N.
items.note: See sourceIssues E7: the proof must intersect with ⟨E, Γ(2N)⟩ before taking the normal core. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Theorem 4.3.1 (the leveraging theorem)
items.statement: Let p ∤ 2N be prime and f(τ) ∈ R_{2N} not invariant under any congruence subgroup. Then f(pτ) (which lies in R_{2Np}, being invariant under A⁻¹G_{2N}A ∩ SL₂(ℤ), of level dividing 2Np by Lemma 4.1.7) is not in the M_{2Np}-algebra generated by R_{2N}.
items.note: Proof: otherwise f(pτ) is invariant under A⁻¹GA ∩ SL₂(ℤ) and G ∩ Γ(2Np), which generate a congruence subgroup by (4.4.10). Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Theorem 4.3.2 (degrees at least double)
items.statement: If p ∤ 2N is prime and [R_{2N} : M_{2N}] > 1 then [R_{2Np} : M_{2Np}] ≥ 2[R_{2N} : M_{2N}].
items.note: Uses R_{2N} ∩ M_{2Np} = M_{2N} and the Galois property of the extensions over ℂ. See sourceIssues E5. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: The degree formula (4.3.3) and bound (4.3.4)
items.note: Mathlib has Γ(N) but not its index ([SL₂(ℤ) : Γ(N)] = N³∏_{p|N}(1 − p⁻²)). Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Proposition 4.3.5 (from an N³ log N bound to the conjecture)
items.statement: If there is C with [R_{2N} : M₂] ≤ C N³ log N for all N, then R_{2N} = M_{2N} for every N; that is, the unbounded denominators conjecture holds.
items.locator: Proposition 4.3.5 and proof, pp.657–658; Remark 4.3.8, p.658 (JAMS 38 (2025))
items.note: Iterating Theorem 4.3.2 over the primes p < X prime to 2N gives degree ≥ 2^{#S}, against ≤ (Cπ²/4)X(1+ε). A bound N^{3+ε} would not suffice. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Prime counting bounds used in Proposition 4.3.5
items.statement: #{p < X} ≫ X/log X and Σ_{p<X} log p ≪ X (the paper quotes the prime number theorem; Chebyshev's bounds suffice).
items.note: Read at 082e2d3: Mathlib/NumberTheory/Chebyshev.lean:481 (ψ(n) ≥ n log 2 − log(n+1)), :293 (ψ(n) ≤ π(n) log n), :194 (θ(x) ≤ x log 4).

items.name: Lemma 4.4.1 (Serre, Berger: a nonabelian Ihara lemma)
items.statement: Let G ⊂ ⟨E, Γ(N)⟩ be normal of finite index in SL₂(ℤ) with L(G) = N, S := ⟨E, Γ(N)⟩/G with projection f, p ∤ N prime and A = diag(p, 1). With f₁(x) = f(x) and f₂(x) = f(AxA⁻¹) on ⟨E, Γ(N)⟩ ∩ Γ₀(p), the map (f₁, f₂) : ⟨E, Γ(N)⟩ ∩ Γ₀(p) → S × S is surjective.
items.locator: §4.4 and Lemma 4.4.1 with proof, pp.658–659 (JAMS 38 (2025)); [Tho89, Theorem 3], [Ber94]
items.note: Proof by Goursat's lemma, the amalgam presentation of the level-N subgroup of SL₂(ℤ[1/p]), its congruence subgroup property and Wohlfahrt's theorem. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Goursat's lemma
items.statement: A subgroup of G × H not surjecting onto a product of its projections is detected by a common nontrivial quotient: subgroups are graphs of isomorphisms G′/M ≅ H′/N.
items.note: Read at 082e2d3: Mathlib/GroupTheory/Goursat.lean:128.

items.name: The amalgam presentation of the level-N subgroup of SL₂(ℤ[1/p])
items.statement: For p ∤ N the natural map ⟨E, Γ(N)⟩ ∗_{⟨E,Γ(N)⟩∩Γ₀(p)} A⁻¹⟨E, Γ(N)⟩A → {g ∈ SL₂(ℤ[1/p]) : g ≡ ±I mod N} is an isomorphism (Ihara's theorem via the Bruhat–Tits tree; [Ber94, p.919], [Ser80], [Tho89, Theorem 3]).
items.locator: proof of Lemma 4.4.1, p.659; proof of Lemma 4.6.2, p.666 (JAMS 38 (2025))
items.note: Mathlib has amalgamated products (GroupTheory/PushoutI.lean:60) but not this isomorphism. Routed as a source of ModularCurvesPartII R14.4, whose Ihara-lemma proof uses this tree geometry.

items.name: The congruence subgroup property of SL₂(ℤ[1/p])
items.statement: Every finite-index subgroup of SL₂(ℤ[1/p]) contains a principal congruence subgroup {g : g ≡ I mod M} for some M prime to p ([Men67], [Ser70]).
items.locator: proof of Lemma 4.4.1, p.659; proof of Lemma 4.6.2, p.666 (JAMS 38 (2025))
items.note: Not planned anywhere in the atlas (KTheoryLowDegrees U.4 plans Bass–Milnor–Serre SK₁(O_{F,S}) = 0, not the SL₂ case). Routed as a source of ModularCurvesPartII R14.4.

items.name: Lemma 4.4.4 (adding the Borel quotient)
items.statement: With B ⊂ SL₂(𝔽_p) the upper-triangular Borel subgroup and π reduction mod p, (f₁, f₂, π) : ⟨E, Γ(N)⟩ ∩ Γ₀(p) → S × S × B is surjective.
items.locator: Lemma 4.4.4 and proof, pp.659–660; Remark 4.4.8, p.660 (JAMS 38 (2025))
items.note: Uses γ = (1 N; 0 1), which lies in ker f₁ ∩ ker f₂ and maps onto the unipotent radical, then the enhanced Ihara lemma (Lemma 4.6.3). See sourceIssues E6 on the kernel of π. Remark 4.4.8: under gcd((p−1)/2, |S|) = 1 the proof is immediate and §§4.5–4.6 are not needed. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: (4.4.9)–(4.4.10): generation of ⟨E, Γ(N)⟩ ∩ Γ₀(p)
items.statement: ⟨E, G ∩ Γ(Np), A⁻¹GA ∩ Γ₀(p)⟩ = ⟨E, Γ(N)⟩ ∩ Γ₀(p); for G = G_{2N}: ⟨E, G ∩ Γ(2Np), A⁻¹GA ∩ Γ₀(p)⟩ = ⟨E, Γ(2N)⟩ ∩ Γ₀(p).
items.note: See sourceIssues E6: the deduction is valid on Γ(N) ∩ Γ₀(p). Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Inflation–restriction in degree 1
items.statement: For a normal subgroup S ⊴ G and a G-module A, 0 → H¹(G/S, A^S) → H¹(G, A) → H¹(S, A) is exact.
items.locator: proofs of Lemma 4.4.4, Corollary 4.5.3 and (4.5.10), pp.659–663 (JAMS 38 (2025))
items.note: Read at 082e2d3: Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/GroupCohomology/Functoriality.lean:393; the inflation map is injective by the instance at :378.

items.name: Definition 4.5.1 (congruence completion and congruence classes)
items.statement: For a congruence subgroup Γ ⊂ SL₂(ℤ), Γ̂ = lim Γ/Γ′ over normal congruence subgroups Γ′; η ∈ H¹(Γ, 𝔽_ℓ) is a congruence class if it restricts to 0 on some congruence subgroup Γ′ ⊂ Γ; the congruence classes form H^{1,cong}(Γ, 𝔽_ℓ) ≅ H¹(Γ̂, 𝔽_ℓ).
items.note: Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Completed cohomology over all levels, H̃¹(𝔽_ℓ)
items.statement: H̃¹(𝔽_ℓ) := lim_N H¹(Γ(N), 𝔽_ℓ) and H̃¹(ℚ/ℤ) := lim_N H¹(Γ(N), ℚ/ℤ) (direct limits over all levels N), with the action of SL₂(Ẑ) = ∏_p SL₂(ℤ_p); the kernel of H¹(Γ(N), 𝔽_ℓ) → H̃¹(𝔽_ℓ) is the congruence classes.
items.note: CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.0–CC.2 plans towers at a fixed prime p with tame level fixed; the colimit over all levels with its SL₂(Ẑ)-action is not planned. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Theorem 4.5.2 (no invariant vectors in completed cohomology)
items.statement: For every prime ℓ the SL₂(Ẑ)-invariant subspace of H̃¹(𝔽_ℓ) is trivial; hence so is that of H̃¹(ℚ/ℤ).
items.note: Proof: H¹(SL₂(Ẑ), 𝔽_ℓ) ≅ H¹(SL₂(ℤ), 𝔽_ℓ), so an invariant class is seen in H²(SL₂(Ẑ), 𝔽_ℓ), which vanishes for ℓ > 5; for ℓ ∈ {3, 5} take N = ℓ and for ℓ = 2 take N = 8 then 16 in (4.5.10), and use Lemma 4.5.11. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Corollary 4.5.3
items.statement: If η ∈ H¹(Γ(N), 𝔽_ℓ) and gη − η is a congruence class for every g ∈ SL₂(ℤ/N), then η is a congruence class.
items.note: Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Lemma 4.5.4 (H₂(SL₂(𝔽_p), ℤ) = 0)
items.statement: H₂(SL₂(𝔽_p), ℤ) = 0 for every prime p.
items.note: Proof via Sylow subgroups: cyclic for odd primes, generalized quaternion for 2 when p is odd. Mathlib has H₂ (GroupHomology/LowDegree.lean:1063) and Tau Ceti the Schur multiplier H²(G, k^×); the computation for SL₂(𝔽_p) is absent. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Lemma 4.5.5 (low-degree cohomology of SL₂(𝔽_p))
items.statement: For n = 1, 2: Hⁿ(SL₂(𝔽_p), 𝔽_ℓ)^∨ ≅ H_n(SL₂(𝔽_p), 𝔽_ℓ) = 𝔽_ℓ if p = ℓ ∈ {2, 3}, and 0 otherwise.
items.note: From Lemma 4.5.4, the universal coefficient sequence and SL₂(𝔽_p)^ab = 1 (p ≥ 5), ℤ/2 (p = 2), ℤ/3 (p = 3). Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Universal coefficients and Sylow reduction for finite groups
items.statement: For a finite group G: H^{n+1}(G, ℤ) ≅ Ext¹(H_n(G, ℤ), ℤ) (n ≥ 0); 0 → H_n(G, ℤ)/ℓ → H_n(G, 𝔽_ℓ) → H_{n−1}(G, ℤ)[ℓ] → 0 and H₁(G, 𝔽_ℓ) ≅ H₁(G, ℤ)/ℓ; the ℓ-primary part of H_n(G, ℤ) injects into H_n of a Sylow ℓ-subgroup; H_n(ℤ/m, ℤ) = 0 for even n > 0; generalized quaternion groups have Hⁿ(Q, ℤ) = 0 for odd n ([Hup67, Satz V.25.3(a)], [Swa60, Theorem 2]).
items.note: Not in Mathlib at the pin. Routed as a source of ArithmeticGaloisDuality D7, the atlas's generic owner of coefficient comparisons for group cohomology beyond upstream ProfiniteCohomology.

items.name: Lemma 4.5.6 (n = 1): H¹(SL₂(ℤ_p), 𝔽_ℓ)
items.statement: H¹(SL₂(ℤ_p), 𝔽_ℓ) = 𝔽_ℓ if p = ℓ ∈ {2, 3}, and 0 otherwise.
items.note: See sourceIssues E11: the case p = ℓ = 2 is not treated in the proof. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Lemma 4.5.6 (n = 2): vanishing of H²(SL₂(ℤ_p), 𝔽_ℓ)
items.statement: H²(SL₂(ℤ_p), 𝔽_ℓ) = 0 unless ℓ = p and p ≤ 5. For ℓ ≠ p, Hochschild–Serre gives H*(SL₂(ℤ_p), 𝔽_ℓ) ≅ H*(SL₂(𝔽_p), 𝔽_ℓ); for ℓ = p ≥ 3 there is an exact sequence 0 → H²(SL₂(𝔽_p), 𝔽_p) → H²(SL₂(ℤ_p), 𝔽_p) → H¹(SL₂(𝔽_p), M) (4.5.8), M = M₀(𝔽_p)^∨.
items.note: Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: The Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for profinite groups
items.statement: For a closed normal subgroup H of a profinite group G and a discrete G-module A: E₂^{i,j} = Hⁱ(G/H, H^j(H, A)) ⇒ H^{i+j}(G, A), with its five-term exact sequence.
items.locator: proofs of Lemmas 4.5.6 and 4.5.9, pp.662–663; diagram (4.5.10), p.663 (JAMS 38 (2025))
items.note: ArithmeticGaloisDuality D7 declares itself the owner of full continuous Hochschild–Serre; R02.2 builds the spectral sequence. Tau Ceti has continuous inflation–restriction (RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/Inflation.lean:336).

items.name: Lazard's theorem for p-powerful torsion-free pro-p groups
items.statement: For p > 2 the first congruence subgroup G(p) ⊂ SL₂(ℤ_p) is p-torsion-free and p-powerful, and with M = M₀(𝔽_p)^∨ (G(p)/G(p²) ≅ M₀(𝔽_p), trace-zero matrices) one has H¹(G(p), 𝔽_p) ≅ M and cup product H²(G(p), 𝔽_p) ≅ ∧²M ≅ M; likewise G(N) ⊂ SL₂(ℤ₂) for N ≥ 4 a power of 2 ([Laz65, V.2.2.6.3 and 2.2.7.2]).
items.note: Not in the libraries or the atlas. Routed as a source of NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa NE.0, whose source route takes the primary Lazard results for each homological claim about Iwasawa algebras of p-adic Lie groups (Ext*_{𝔽_p[[G]]}(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p) = H*(G, 𝔽_p)).

items.name: H¹(SL₂(𝔽_p), ad⁰) = 0 for p ≠ 5 ([DDT97, Lemma 2.48])
items.statement: For p ≥ 3 and M ≅ M₀(𝔽_p)^∨ (the adjoint representation on trace-zero matrices), H¹(SL₂(𝔽_p), M) = 0 unless p = 5.
items.note: ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7 plans the enormous-image conditions, which contain H¹(H, ad⁰) = 0, and its integrated node asks to check them for SL₂(𝔽_p), p ≥ 5; the computation itself, with the exception p = 5, is not planned. Routed as a source of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7.

items.name: Lemma 4.5.9(a): reduction of H² to one prime
items.statement: For every prime ℓ: H²(SL₂(Ẑ), 𝔽_ℓ) ≅ H²(SL₂(ℤ_ℓ), 𝔽_ℓ), and for N a power of ℓ with G(N) ⊂ SL₂(ℤ_ℓ) the principal congruence subgroup, H²(Γ̂(N), 𝔽_ℓ) ≅ H²(G(N), 𝔽_ℓ).
items.note: By the Künneth formula and Lemma 4.5.6. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Lemma 4.5.9(b): the restriction H²(SL₂(Ẑ)) → H²(Γ̂(N)) vanishes
items.statement: If ℓ is odd and N a nontrivial power of ℓ, or ℓ = 2 and N ≥ 8 a power of 2, then H²(SL₂(Ẑ), 𝔽_ℓ) → H²(Γ̂(N), 𝔽_ℓ) is zero.
items.note: Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Künneth formula for mod-ℓ cohomology of products of profinite groups
items.statement: For profinite groups G₁, G₂ with finite H^i(G_j, 𝔽_ℓ): Hⁿ(G₁ × G₂, 𝔽_ℓ) ≅ ⊕_{i+j=n} H^i(G₁, 𝔽_ℓ) ⊗ H^j(G₂, 𝔽_ℓ); applied to SL₂(Ẑ) = ∏_p SL₂(ℤ_p) and Γ̂(N) in degrees ≤ 2.
items.locator: proofs of Lemma 4.5.9 and Theorem 4.5.2, pp.663–664 (JAMS 38 (2025))
items.note: Not planned (the Künneth statements in the atlas concern étale, crystalline or singular cohomology). Routed as a source of ArithmeticGaloisDuality D7.

items.name: The comparison diagram (4.5.10)
items.statement: For N ∈ {3, 4, 5, 8, 16} and ℓ | N, compatible Hochschild–Serre sequences give a commutative diagram with exact rows H¹(SL₂(Ẑ)) ↪ H¹(SL₂(ℤ)) → (H̃¹(𝔽_ℓ))^{SL₂(Ẑ)} → H²(SL₂(Ẑ)) → H²(SL₂(ℤ)) and H¹(Γ̂(N)) ↪ H¹(Γ(N)) → (H̃¹(𝔽_ℓ))^{Γ̂(N)} → H²(Γ̂(N)) → 0 (𝔽_ℓ coefficients), the last map onto 0 because Γ(N) is free.
items.note: Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Γ(N) is free for N ≥ 3
items.statement: For N ≥ 3, Γ(N) is torsion-free and is the fundamental group of the punctured surface ℍ/Γ(N), hence free; Γ(8) and Γ(16) are free of ranks 33 and 257, and H²(Γ(N), 𝔽_ℓ) = 0.
items.locator: (4.5.10) discussion, p.663; proof of Lemma 4.5.11, p.664 (JAMS 38 (2025))
items.note: FuchsianOrbifolds Layer 2 derives the standard presentation of a cofinite Fuchsian group from a fundamental polygon, which for a torsion-free group with cusps is free of rank 2g + c − 1. Mathlib has Nielsen–Schreier (GroupTheory/FreeGroup/NielsenSchreier.lean:321).

items.name: Lemma 4.5.11 (invariants in H¹(Γ(N), 𝔽_ℓ) for N = 3, 4, 5, 8, 16)
items.statement: dim H¹(Γ(3), 𝔽₃)^{SL₂(𝔽₃)} = 0; dim H¹(Γ(5), 𝔽₅)^{SL₂(𝔽₅)} = 0 (printed with 𝔽₃, see sourceIssues E1); dim H¹(Γ(N), 𝔽₂)^{SL₂(ℤ/N)} = 1 for N = 4, 8, 16. For N = 3, 4, 5 the same holds for the semisimplifications.
items.note: For N = 3, 4, 5 (genus 0) the module is Q[PSL₂(ℤ/N)/⟨U⟩] − [Q], analysed through Brauer characters of A₄, S₄, A₅; N = 8, 16 are machine computations (magma) on free groups of ranks 33 and 257. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Lemma 4.5.12 (low-degree cohomology of SL₂(ℤ_p))
items.statement: For n = 1, 2: Hⁿ(SL₂(ℤ_p), 𝔽_ℓ) = 𝔽_ℓ if p = ℓ ∈ {2, 3}, and 0 otherwise; H₂(SL₂(ℤ_p), ℤ) = 0 for all p.
items.note: Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Cohomology of SL₂(ℤ) and its completions
items.statement: Hⁿ(SL₂(ℤ), ℤ) = ℤ/12 for even n > 0 and 0 for odd n; H¹(SL₂(ℤ), 𝔽_ℓ) ≅ ℤ/12 ⊗ 𝔽_ℓ and H¹(SL₂(Ẑ), 𝔽_ℓ) → H¹(SL₂(ℤ), 𝔽_ℓ) is an isomorphism; H₁(SL₂(ℤ_p), ℤ) ≅ ℤ/12 ⊗ ℤ_p.
items.locator: proofs of Theorem 4.5.2 and Lemma 4.5.12, pp.664–665 (JAMS 38 (2025))
items.note: Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Lemma 4.6.2 (Ihara's lemma, Ribet)
items.statement: Let q be prime, N ≥ 3 and (N, p) = 1. The kernel of H¹(Γ(N), 𝔽_q)² → H¹(Γ(N) ∩ Γ₀(p), 𝔽_q), (ψ, φ) ↦ ψ − Aφ with (Aφ)(g) = φ(AgA⁻¹), lies in H^{1,cong}(Γ(N), 𝔽_q)².
items.note: The abelian case of Lemma 4.4.1. ModularCurvesPartII R14.4 plans Ihara's lemma in the modular-curve settings of level raising, by tree geometry; this Γ(N) form with congruence classes is not among them. Routed as a source of ModularCurvesPartII R14.4.

items.name: Lemma 4.6.3 (enhanced Ihara lemma)
items.statement: The kernel of the composite of (4.6.1) with restriction H¹(Γ(N) ∩ Γ₀(p), 𝔽_q) → H¹(Γ(N) ∩ Γ₁(p), 𝔽_q) also lies in H^{1,cong}(Γ(N), 𝔽_q)².
items.note: SL₂(ℤ/N) acts trivially on the kernel of (4.6.4), so (ψ^g − ψ, φ^g − φ) lies in the Ihara kernel; then Corollary 4.5.3. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Uniformization (conformal) radius of a pointed hyperbolic plane domain
items.statement: For an open U ⊂ ℂ containing 0 whose complement in ℂ has at least two points, the uniformization radius of (U, 0) is |F′(0)| for a holomorphic universal covering F : D(0,1) → U with F(0) = 0 (independent of F, which is unique up to rotation); for U = ℂ∖μ_N it is the conformal size |F_N′(0)|.
items.note: Tau Ceti has normalized Riemann maps of simply connected domains with their derivative at the base point (Conformal/RiemannMapping/Normalization.lean:122); the multiply connected case needs the universal covering. Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Holomorphic universal coverings of punctured planes
items.statement: For distinct a₁,…,a_n ∈ ℂ with n ≥ 2 there is a holomorphic covering map D(0,1) → ℂ∖{a₁,…,a_n}, unique up to automorphisms of the disc, with deck group a Fuchsian group; equivalently F̃ : ℍ → ℍ/Γ̃ ≅ ℂ∖{a_i}. For μ_N it can be built by Schwarz reflection of the Riemann map of the symmetric circular 2N-gon with zero angles ([Gol69, §§II.6, III.1]).
items.note: Tau Ceti has the topological universal cover, the Riemann mapping theorem (Conformal/RiemannMapping/Existence.lean:69), Schwarz reflection and the monodromy theorem, but no holomorphic uniformization of multiply connected plane domains. Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: The Schwarz lemma for uniformization radii
items.statement: If U ⊂ ℂ is a hyperbolic domain containing 0 and φ : D(0,1) → U is holomorphic with φ(0) = 0, then |φ′(0)| ≤ |F′(0)| for the universal covering F with F(0) = 0 (lift φ through F and apply the Schwarz lemma), with equality only if φ is a universal covering.
items.note: Mathlib has the Schwarz lemma (Analysis/Complex/Schwarz.lean:261). Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: The Cayley transform D(0,1) ≅ ℍ
items.statement: z ↦ i(1 + z)/(1 − z) is a conformal isomorphism D(0,1) → ℍ sending 0 to i; PSL₂(ℝ) and PSU(1,1) correspond under it (Remark 5.0.1: tilde notation for objects on ℍ).
items.note: Read at f790474: TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/UpperHalfPlane/DiscCoordinate.lean:119, the equivalence ℍ ≃ 𝔻 given by τ ↦ (τ − z)/(τ − z̄) with inverse w ↦ (z − z̄w)/(1 − w); at z = i this is the Cayley transform used here.

items.name: Definition 5.1.1 (the normalized uniformization F_N of ℂ∖μ_N)
items.statement: For N ≥ 2, F̃_N : ℍ → ℍ/Γ̃_N = ℂ∖μ_N is the universal covering normalized so that i∞ is a cusp with F̃_N(i∞) = 1 and F̃_N(i) = 0 (Γ̃_N ⊂ PSL₂(ℝ) its Fuchsian group); F_N(z) := F̃_N(i(1+z)/(1−z)), so F_N : D(0,1) → ℂ∖μ_N is the universal covering with F_N(0) = 0 and F_N(1) = 1.
items.note: Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Lemma 5.1.2 (rotational symmetry of F_N)
items.statement: ζ_N F̃_N(τ) = F̃_N(r̃_N·τ) with r̃_N = (cos(π/N) −sin(π/N); sin(π/N) cos(π/N)) ∈ PSO₂(ℝ), a rotation of order N about i, and F_N(ζz) = ζF_N(z) for every ζ ∈ μ_N.
items.note: Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Theorem 5.1.4 (the conformal radius of ℂ∖μ_N; Kraus–Roth)
items.locator: Theorem 5.1.4 and (5.1.5), p.668; proof pp.672–673 (JAMS 38 (2025)); [KR16, Remark 5.1]
items.note: Both forms and Example 5.1.22's values were checked numerically here (N = 2, 3, 4, 5, 10, 50). Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Theorem 5.1.4, the expansion (5.1.6)
items.note: The series and the positivity of the remainder were checked numerically here. Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: The Schwarzian derivative and Poincaré's equation (Remark 5.1.10)
items.statement: {w, x} := (w″/w′)′ − ½(w″/w′)², invariant under Möbius transformations of w; a function w is locally the quotient v₁/v₂ of two independent solutions of y″ + ½{w, x}y = 0 (v₁ = w/√w′, v₂ = 1/√w′) ([dSG16, §IV.1.2, Prop. VIII.3.5]).
items.note: Also missing in PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19's extraction. Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Hempel's theorem on the Schwarzian of an inverse uniformization
items.statement: For a finite S = {p₀,…,p_N} ⊂ ℂ (so ∞ ∉ S) and the universal covering ℍ → ℙ¹∖S, with multivalued inverse τ: {τ, X} = ½Σ_k (X − p_k)⁻² + Σ_k m_k/(X − p_k) with accessory parameters subject to Σm_k = 0, Σ(2m_k p_k + 1) = 0, Σ(m_k p_k² + p_k) = 0 (vanishing to order four at ∞), and the local inverse is a ratio of two independent solutions of y″ + ½{τ, X}y = 0 ([Hem88, Theorem 3.1, Lemma 3.3]).
items.note: Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Lemma 5.1.8 (the Schwarzian equation of ℂ∖μ_N)
items.statement: The local inverse ψ_N of F_N with ψ_N(0) = 0 is η₁/η₂ (up to a Möbius transformation) for solutions of 4(x^N − 1)²y″ + ((N² − 1)x^{N−2} + x^{2N−2})y = 0 (5.1.9); equivalently {τ, F̃_N} = ((N² − 1)x^{N−2} + x^{2N−2})/(2(x^N − 1)²), the μ_N-symmetry forcing the accessory parameters m₀ = 0 and m_k = −(½ + 1/2N)ζ_N^{−k}.
items.note: The Schwarzian identity, the three constraints and (5.1.9) were checked numerically here for N = 2, 3, 5, 8. Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Definition 5.1.15 (the map G_N)
items.statement: G_N : D(0,1) → ℂ∖{1} with G_N(z^N) = F_N(z)^N, i.e. G_N(z) = F_N(z^{1/N})^N (well defined by Lemma 5.1.2).
items.note: Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Lemma 5.1.16 (the hypergeometric inverse of G_N)
items.statement: The local inverse φ_N of G_N (φ_N(0) = 0) is δ_N⁻¹(φ₁/φ₂)^N with φ₁ = √(1−x)·x^{1/N}·₂F₁((N+1)/2N, (N+1)/2N; 1 + 1/N; x) and φ₂ = √(1−x)·₂F₁((N−1)/2N, (N−1)/2N; 1 − 1/N; x), solutions of x(x−1)²y″ + (1 − 1/N)(x−1)²y′ + (¼ + (x−1)/(4N²))y = 0; with s_N(x) := x^{1/N}·₂F₁(…;1+1/N;x)/₂F₁(…;1−1/N;x): φ_N = δ_N⁻¹s_N^N, ψ_N(x) = |F_N′(0)|⁻¹s_N(x^N) and δ_N = |G_N′(0)| = |F_N′(0)|^N.
items.note: Mathlib has ₂F₁ as a power series but not the hypergeometric equation. The ODE (5.1.17) and its composition with x^N were checked numerically here. Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Lemma 5.1.20 (₂F₁(a,a;2a;·) near 1; [AS92, 15.3.10])
items.statement: For a ∉ ℤ_{≤0} and |x| < 1: ₂F₁(a, a; 2a; 1 − x) = (Γ(2a)/Γ(a)²) Σ_{k≥0} ((a)_k²/k!²) x^k (−log x + 2(ψ(k+1) − ψ(k+a))), ψ = Γ′/Γ, all branches accounted for by the branches of log.
items.note: Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Gamma and digamma identities used in §5
items.statement: The duplication formula Γ(s)Γ(s + ½) = 2^{1−2s}√π Γ(2s) ([AS92, 6.1.18]); the reflection formulas Γ(z)Γ(1−z) = π/sin(πz) and ψ(1 − s) = ψ(s) + π cot(πs) ([AS92, 6.3.7]); ψ(1) = −γ.
items.locator: proofs of Theorem 5.1.4 and Lemma 5.2.12, pp.673, 677 (JAMS 38 (2025))
items.note: Read at 082e2d3: Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gamma/Beta.lean:559 and :398; Gamma/Digamma.lean:94 and :56 (digamma 1 = −eulerMascheroniConstant).

items.name: The Taylor series of log Γ with zeta values ([AS92, 6.1.33])
items.statement: log Γ(1 + z) = −γz + Σ_{k≥2} (−1)^k ζ(k) z^k/k for |z| < 1, which gives the series for log γ_N in (5.1.6).
items.note: Mathlib has Γ, ζ and the Bohr–Mollerup log-Gamma sequence but not this series. Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Example 5.1.22 (N = 2 and N = 3)
items.statement: F₂(z) = 2λ(i(1−z)/(1+z)) − 1 uniformizes ℂ∖{±1} and |F₂′(0)| = Γ(1/4)⁴/(4π²) = 4.37687923… > √16; F₃ is an explicit η-quotient of a Möbius transform of z and |F₃′(0)| = Γ(1/6)³/(12π^{3/2}) = 2.5810565… > ∛16; ℂ∖μ_N ≅ Y(N) only for N = 2, 3.
items.note: Links the λ-function to F₂; the constants were checked numerically here. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms, which owns λ.

items.name: Proposition 5.2.1 (the Fuchsian group of ℂ∖μ_N)
items.statement: The stabilizer of i∞ in Γ̃_N is generated by t̃_N = (1 2cot(π/2N); 0 1); Γ̃_N is free on t̃_N and its conjugates by the powers of r̃_N; a fundamental domain in D(0,1) is the ideal 2N-gon with cusps at the half-integer powers ζ_N^{k/2} bounded by the geodesics joining adjacent cusps (the Dirichlet domain at 0).
items.note: Tau Ceti has the hyperbolic distance on the disc (Conformal/Hyperbolic/Distance.lean:68); Dirichlet domains are planned in FuchsianOrbifolds Layer 2 in general. Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Definition 5.2.3 (the group Φ̃_N)
items.statement: Φ̃_N := ⟨Γ̃_N, r̃_N⟩ = ⟨r̃_N, t̃_N⟩ ⊂ PSL₂(ℝ), with Φ_N the corresponding lattice in PSU(1,1).
items.note: Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Corollary 5.2.4 (the symmetry group of F_N^N)
items.statement: F̃_N^N is invariant under Φ̃_N, the largest subgroup of PSL₂(ℝ) with this property; a fundamental domain Ω′_N for Φ_N in D(0,1) is the hyperbolic quadrilateral with vertices 0, ζ_N^{−1/2}, 1, ζ_N^{1/2} (in ℍ: geodesics i → cot(π/2N) → i∞ → −cot(π/2N) → i).
items.note: Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Lemma 5.2.6 (the involution exchanging the cusps of F_N^N)
items.statement: For s̃ ∈ PSL₂(ℝ) a rotation of order 2N with s̃² = r̃_N: 1 − F̃_N^N(s̃·τ) = 1/(1 − F̃_N^N(τ)).
items.note: Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Remark 5.2.8 (the (N, ∞, ∞) triangle group)
items.statement: Φ̃_N has index two in Ψ̃_N = ⟨s̃, t̃_N⟩, whose fundamental domain is the hyperbolic triangle 0, 1, ζ_N^{1/2} with angles {π/N, 0, 0}; so F_N^N is expressed through Schwarz triangle functions ([Car54, §404]).
items.note: Triangle groups with cusp parameters are planned in FuchsianOrbifolds Layer 2 (item 6); the identification of this one with the symmetry group of F_N^N is routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Lemma 5.2.9 (asymptotics of s_N near 1)
items.statement: Fix M₀ > 0. For M ≥ M₀ and |x| < e^{−MN}: |s_N(1−x)/γ_N − (1−x)^{1/N}·(−log x − 2γ − 2ψ(½ + 1/2N))/(−log x − 2γ − 2ψ(½ − 1/2N))| ≪ |x|/N, γ Euler's constant and the implicit constant depending only on M₀.
items.note: Stated with the sign of γ corrected; the source prints +2γ (sourceIssues E2). Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Lemma 5.2.12 (the cusp horoball where F_N^N ≈ 1)
items.statement: Fix M₀ > 0 and ε > 0. For M ≥ M₀ and τ in the fundamental domain Ω̃′_N ⊂ ℍ with |F̃_N(τ)^N − 1| < e^{−MN}: Im τ > 2N²M(1 − ε)/π² once N ≫_{ε,M₀} 1.
items.note: Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Lemma 5.2.16 (images of horoballs in the disc)
items.statement: For γ ∈ PSU(1,1) with image (a b; c d) ∈ PSL₂(ℝ), the image in D(0,1) of the horoball {Im τ ≥ D} is the disc of diameter E(γ, D) = 2/(1 + D(a² + c²)) tangent to 𝕋 at (a − ic)/(a + ic).
items.note: Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Shimizu's lemma
items.statement: If a discrete subgroup of PSL₂(ℝ) contains τ ↦ τ + h (h > 0), then |c| ≥ 1/h for each of its elements (a b; c d) with c ≠ 0 ([EGM98, Theorem 3.1]); for Γ̃_N and Φ̃_N this gives 2(|a| + |c|)cot(π/2N) ≥ 1.
items.note: FuchsianOrbifolds Layer 3 plans precisely invariant horodiscs but not this quantitative bound. Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution, stated for discrete subgroups of PSL₂(ℝ).

items.name: Lemma 5.2.18 (crude growth bound for F_N)
items.statement: For N ≫ 1 and r ∈ (0,1): sup_{|z|=r} log|F_N(z)| ≪ N/(1 − r), with absolute implicit constants.
items.locator: Lemma 5.2.18 and proof, p.678; Remark 5.2.19 (JAMS 38 (2025)); [KR16, Theorems 1.2, 1.10]
items.note: See sourceIssues E9 for a slip in the proof. Remark 5.2.19: the supremum method alone gives only an O(N⁴) holonomy bound. Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Theorem 6.0.1 (uniform mean growth of F_N)
items.statement: For p(x) ∈ {x^N, x^N/(x^N − 1), 1/(x^N − 1)} and uniformly in N ≥ 2 and r ∈ (0,1): ∫_{|z|=r} log⁺|p∘F_N| dμ_Haar ≪ log(N/(1 − r)), with an effectively computable absolute constant.
items.note: The statement says N ∈ ℕ_{>0}; the section assumes N ≥ 2, where F_N exists. Tsuji's asymptotic (1/(N−1))log(1/(1−r)) is not uniform in N. Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: The mean proximity function m(r, f)
items.note: Read at 082e2d3: Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/ValueDistribution/Proximity/Basic.lean:50, `proximity f ⊤ = circleAverage (log⁺ ‖f ·‖) 0`, defined for every f : ℂ → E; so it serves functions on the disc for r < 1, though Mathlib's API about it assumes f meromorphic on ℂ.

items.name: The counting function N(r, f) on the disc
items.statement: For f meromorphic on D(0,1) and 0 < r < 1: N(r, f) = N(r, f; ∞) := Σ_{0<|ρ|<r} ord⁻_ρ(f) log(r/|ρ|) + ord⁻₀(f) log r, with ord⁻_ρ(f) := max(0, ord_ρ(1/f)) the pole order.
items.note: Near miss: Mathlib's `logCounting` (ValueDistribution/LogCounting/Basic.lean:354) uses the divisor of f on all of ℂ, so it presupposes f meromorphic on ℂ. Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: The Nevanlinna characteristic T(r, f) on the disc
items.statement: T(r, f) := m(r, f) + N(r, f) for f meromorphic on D(0,1) and 0 < r < 1.
items.note: Near miss: Mathlib's `characteristic` (ValueDistribution/CharacteristicFunction.lean:53) is the plane version. Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Lemma 6.1.2(a) (nonnegativity of N(r, f))
items.statement: For f meromorphic on D(0,1), regular at 0, and r ∈ (0,1): N(r, f) ≥ 0, with equality iff f is holomorphic on D(0, r).
items.note: Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Lemma 6.1.2(b) (Nevanlinna's first main theorem on the disc)
items.statement: For a ∈ ℂ: |T(r, f) − T(r, 1/(f − a)) − log|c(f, a)|| ≤ log⁺|a| + log 2, c(f, a) := lim_{z→0}(f(z) − a)z^{−ord₀(f−a)}; including (6.1.4) T(r, f) − T(r, 1/f) = log|c(f, 0)| (Poisson–Jensen) and (6.1.5) |log⁺|f − a| − log⁺|f|| ≤ log⁺|a| + log 2.
items.note: Near miss: Mathlib's first main theorem (ValueDistribution/FirstMainTheorem.lean:47–161) is stated for f meromorphic on ℂ; Jensen's formula itself is local (item jensen-formula). Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Lemma 6.1.7 (logarithmic derivative lemma for zero-free functions)
items.statement: If g is holomorphic and zero-free on a neighbourhood of D̄(0,R) with g(0) = 1, then for 0 < r < R: m(r, g′/g) < log⁺{(m(R, g)/r)·R/(R − r)} + log 2 + 1/e.
items.note: The general meromorphic version (Goldberg–Grinshtein (6.1.14), constant 5.8501) is cited but not used. Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Corollary 6.2.9
items.statement: For f = 1 − F_N^N: m(r, f′/f) ≪ sup_{|z|=(1+r)/2} log⁺ log|F_N| + log(N/(1 − r)).
items.note: Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Corollary 6.2.11
items.statement: m(r, F_N/F_N′) ≤ T(r, F_N) + O(log⁺(N/(1 − r)) + sup_{|z|=(1+r)/2} log⁺ log|F_N|).
items.note: Uses that F_N′ never vanishes (F_N is étale) and |F_N′(0)| > 1; see sourceIssues E8 for the radius in the proof. Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: The pivot identity (6.2.4), (6.2.7) and the lower bound (6.2.3)
items.statement: x^N/(x^N − 1) = (x/N)Σ_{ζ∈μ_N} 1/(x − ζ); hence p∘F_N = (F_N/(N F_N′))·(f′/f) for p(x) = x^N/(x^N − 1) and f = 1 − F_N^N; and T(r, p∘F_N) ≥ N·T(r, F_N) − log 4, the three choices of p in Theorem 6.0.1 being equivalent.
items.note: The special feature of μ_N exploited here is that ∏(x − ζ) = x^N − 1 has N^{O(1)} coefficients. Routed to PuncturedPlaneUniformizationAndValueDistribution.

items.name: Theorem 7.2.1 (algebraicity of integral ODE solutions with finite local monodromy)
items.statement: If f(x) ∈ ℤ[[x]] satisfies L(f) = 0 for a linear differential operator L without singularities on ℙ¹∖{0, 1/16, ∞} (or with only trivially-monodromic ones there), and the local monodromy of L at x = 0 is finite, then f is algebraic over ℚ(x).
items.note: With monodromy ℤ/N, g(x) = f(x^N) ∈ H(ℂ∖16^{−1/N}μ_N, ℤ) and Corollary 2.0.5 applies with φ(z) = 16^{−1/N}F_N(rz), 16^{1/N}/|F_N′(0)| < r < 1. Answers the question of [And04, Appendix, A.5]. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Theorem 7.2.1 (congruence automorphy of such solutions)
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 7.2.1, f(λ(τ)/16) is automorphic for some principal congruence subgroup Γ(M), M ≡ 0 mod N; for Puiseux series the same holds with f(λ(τ)/16) ∈ ℤ[[λ(τ/m)/16]] ⊗ ℂ in place of f ∈ ℤ[[x]] (Remark 7.2.2).
items.locator: Theorem 7.2.1 and proof, pp.687–688; Remark 7.2.2, p.688 (JAMS 38 (2025))
items.note: By algebraicity f(λ/16) is automorphic for a finite-index Γ ⊂ Γ(2); Theorem 1.0.1 upgrades it. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Congruence forms of weight k as solutions of linear ODEs in λ/16
items.statement: A congruence modular form of weight k > 0, expanded in x = λ(τ)/16, satisfies a linear ODE of order k + 1 over a finite étale cover of ℙ¹∖{0, 1/16, ∞} ≅ Y(2) with monodromy commensurable with Sym^k SL₂(ℤ) ⊂ SL_{k+1}(ℤ) ([Sti84], [Zag08, §5.4]); e.g. Δ; so the finite-monodromy hypothesis of Theorem 7.2.1 is essential.
items.note: Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Definition 7.3.1 (vector-valued modular forms for PSL₂(ℤ))
items.statement: A vector-valued modular form of weight k ∈ ℤ and dimension n is a pair (F, ρ) with F = (F₁,…,F_n) : ℍ → ℂⁿ holomorphic and ρ : PSL₂(ℤ) → GL_n(ℂ) such that F^t|_kγ = ρ(γ)F^t for all γ, ρ((1 1; 0 1)) is semisimple, and each F_j has moderate growth in vertical strips (|F_j(τ)| ≤ Ae^{B Im τ} for a ≤ Re τ ≤ b, Im τ ≥ C).
items.note: Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Remark 7.3.2 (q-expansions of vector-valued forms)
items.statement: Semisimplicity of ρ(T) and moderate growth are together equivalent to generalized Puiseux expansions F_j = Σ_{n≥n₀} a_{n,j}q^{n+μ} without log q terms (after diagonalizing ρ(T), e^{2πiμ} the eigenvalue); scalar modular forms on a finite-index Γ ⊂ PSL₂(ℤ) are first components of vector-valued forms of dimension [Γ(1) : Γ]; Knopp–Mason generalized modular forms are the monomial case.
items.note: Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: The flat bundle on Y(2) attached to a vector-valued modular form
items.statement: For a weight-0 vector-valued form (F, ρ) the ℤ[x, 1/x, 1/(1 − 16x)]-module spanned by the F_j|γ over the six cosets γ of Γ(2) in SL₂(ℤ), with ∇ = d/dx for x = λ/16, is a rank-6n vector bundle with integrable connection (𝓔, ∇) on Y(2), with monodromy ρ|_{Γ(2)} and regular singularities with semisimple local monodromies at the three cusps.
items.note: Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: G-functions
items.statement: A power series Σ aₙxⁿ with coefficients in a number field that satisfies a linear ODE over ℚ̄(x), and such that the houses of the aₙ (maximum absolute value over conjugates) and the common denominators of a₀,…,aₙ grow at most geometrically ([DGS94, p.xiii]).
items.note: DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence DT.5 plans E- and G-functions but has no integrated node yet. Routed as a source of DT.5.

items.name: Chudnovsky's theorem on G-functions
items.statement: The minimal linear differential system satisfied by a G-function satisfies the Galočkin condition (finite global operator height σ(∇) < ∞) ([DGS94, Theorem VIII.1.5]).
items.note: Routed as a source of DT.5.

items.name: The Bombieri–André theorem
items.statement: A linear differential system over ℚ̄(x) satisfying the Galočkin condition satisfies the Bombieri condition (finite generic global inverse radius ρ(∇) < ∞), and is therefore globally nilpotent ([DGS94, Theorem VII.2.1, VII.2.(2.1), (2.3)]).
items.note: Routed as a source of DT.5.

items.name: Katz's local monodromy theorem
items.statement: A globally nilpotent connection has regular singularities with quasi-unipotent local monodromies ([Kat70], [DGS94, Theorem III.2.3(ii)]).
items.note: Routed as a source of DT.5, together with the G-function theorems that feed it.

items.name: Theorem 7.3.3 (unbounded denominators for vector-valued modular forms)
items.statement: Let (F, ρ) be a vector-valued modular form for PSL₂(ℤ) of dimension n and weight k. If some component F_j has Fourier expansion at i∞ in ℤ[[q]] = ℤ[[e^{πiτ}]], then F_j is a classical modular form of weight k on a congruence subgroup of SL₂(ℤ).
items.note: Reduce to weight 0 by F·g·(λ/16Δ(τ/2))^{(k+k′)/12}, restrict to Γ(2), pass to an irreducible local system; the G-function theorems make the local monodromies quasi-unipotent and semisimplicity makes them finite; then Theorem 7.2.1. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Corollary 7.3.4 (Mason's conjecture)
items.statement: If all components of a vector-valued modular form (F, ρ) for PSL₂(ℤ) have Fourier expansions with bounded denominators, then ρ has finite image, and ker ρ ⊇ Γ(N) for some N ∈ ℕ_{>0}.
items.note: Recovers the congruence property of rational conformal field theories [DLN15], [DR18]. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Definition 7.4.3 (weakly holomorphic quasi-modular forms)
items.statement: For Γ ⊂ PSL₂(ℤ): M̃(Γ) = M(Γ)[E₂] is the ring of quasi-modular forms ([Zag08, Prop. 20(ii)]), M^!(Γ) the weakly holomorphic modular forms (meromorphic modular forms holomorphic away from the cusps), and M̃^!(Γ) := M̃(Γ)[1/Δ].
items.note: Mathlib has E₂ and Δ, not the quasi-modular ring; ModularForms Layer 11 puts the quasi-modular E₂ phenomenon out of scope. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Lemma 7.4.4 (the θ-closure of M^!(Γ))
items.statement: M̃^!(Γ) is the smallest ring containing M^!(Γ) and closed under θ = q d/dq = (1/πi)d/dτ (using θΔ = E₂Δ and that M̃(Γ) is θ-stable, [Zag08, Prop. 20(i)]).
items.note: Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: §7.4.2: logarithmic examples supporting Question 7.4.5
items.statement: (2/π)E(λ(q)) := ₂F₁(½, −½; 1; λ) = 1 − 4q + 20q² − 64q³ + 164q⁴ − 392q⁵ + ⋯ = (ϑ₃ϑ₄⁴ + 4θϑ₃)/ϑ₃³ ∈ M̃^!(Γ(12)); (2/π)E(16x) = (1 − 16x)(2/π)K(16x) + 8∫₀ˣ(2/π)K(16t)dt (printed with the opposite sign, sourceIssues E10); ∫₀ˣ(2/π)K(16t)dt = Σ C(2n,n)²x^{n+1}/(n+1) ∈ ℤ[[x]] and Σ C_n² x^{n+1} ∈ ℤ[[x]] (Catalan numbers C_n); and (Zudilin) Σ_{n≥0} C(2n,n)²(λ/16)ⁿ/(n+1)² = (4/ϑ₂⁴)(4ϑ₃²·θϑ₂/ϑ₂ + 4ϑ₃·θϑ₃ − ϑ₃⁴).
items.note: All identities except the printed E–K relation were confirmed here by exact q-series arithmetic. The paper's Question 7.4.5 (whether Z[[q]] components of logarithmic vector-valued forms are weakly holomorphic quasi-modular for a congruence group) stays open. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: §7.4.8: the spaces S_k(ρ) and the deficient places Σ(ρ)
items.statement: For ρ : PSL₂(ℤ) → GL_n(ℂ): S_k(ρ) is the ℚ̄-space of weight-k cuspidal vector-valued forms with multiplier ρ whose components lie in q^{1/N}ℚ̄[[q^{1/N}]] for some N; a place v of ℚ̄ is in Σ(ρ) iff some component f = Σ a_l q^l has |a_l|_∞ l^{−(k−1)/2−ε} unbounded for some ε > 0 (v = ∞) or |a_l|_v unbounded (v finite).
items.note: Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: §7.4.8: congruence kernels have no deficient places, others a finite one
items.statement: If ker ρ is a congruence subgroup then Σ(ρ) = ∅ (Shimura's integrality theorem and Deligne's Ramanujan–Petersson bound); if ker ρ is not a congruence subgroup then Σ(ρ) contains a non-archimedean place (by the proof of Theorem 7.3.3). Selberg: |a_l| = O(l^{k/2−1/5}) for every ρ.
items.note: Whether ∞ ∈ Σ(ρ) can occur, and whether Σ(ρ) is always finite, are left open. Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.

items.name: Theorem 7.4.10 (π₁ of the connected Néron model of X(N))
items.statement: Let N ≥ 1, K/ℚ(μ_N) finite, π : 𝒳(N) → Spec O_K the connected component containing the cusp ∞ of the smooth locus of the minimal regular model of X(N) over O_K, and ε : Spec O_K → 𝒳(N) the extension of ∞. For every geometric point η of Spec O_K, π_* : π₁(𝒳(N), ε(η)) → π₁(Spec O_K, η) and ε_* are mutually inverse isomorphisms.
items.locator: Theorem 7.4.10 and sketch of proof, p.696; Remarks 7.4.11–7.4.12 (JAMS 38 (2025)); [Iha94, §4 and Thm 1]
items.note: Sketch: Ihara's argument with O_K[[λ(τ/N)/16]] in place of Ihara's power series ring and Theorem 1.0.1 with Remark 6.3.1 in place of Harbater's rationality input [Iha94, Claim 1A]; N = 6 follows from [Bos99]. Needs étale fundamental groups (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.0–IG.1) and regular models (ModularCurvesPartII R13.5). Routed to NoncongruenceModularForms.
